text.p: Raytheon Co bid $9 billion for the defence end of General Motors' Hughes Electronics Corp, The Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday, quoting people familiar with the situation.
General Motors also received a slightly higher bid from Northrop Grumman Corp, though the exact amount of that bid was not known, the newspaper reported.
The Journal said Raytheon was told it was outbid by Northrop Grumman by $200 million to $500 million.
Bidding remains open for the Hughes assets and both companies in the running are concerned about overextending themselves if the price goes too high, according to the Journal.

Both companies could have their debt ratings lowered because they would assume between $3 billion and $5 billion in debt as part of the deal to acquire the Hughes missile and defence-electronics holdings, one of the few jewels remaining in the era of post-Cold War defence consolidation, the newspaper said.
Raytheon and Northrop Grumman would each have to put up about $5 billion of its own stock to buy the Hughes unit, the Journal reported.
Raytheon said on Monday it plans to buy the defence operations of Texas Instruments for $2.95 billion in cash.
